Messages.Author: David Gausebeck
Messages.Body:
>How about usable only once per game, by any methusaleh? Makes putting a
>lot of them in and designing a deck around it kinda dumb.

It does have some points in its favor...
It still leaves the card capable of ousting a prey with no warning
from 15-20 pool, and I somehow get the impression that this would make
the change more palatable to the people at WotC.

It does make it somewhat silly to base a deck around it, though, which
should be enough of a fix to keep it from really messing up game
balance.

And it kind of fits in with the other "you get to be cool because you
have big vampires" cards, like ancient influence and whatever the
similar one from Sabbat is.

And it's probably the simplest and most elegant fix I've seen. One
simple alteration. Nothing complicated or confusing. Also makes it
seem more likely that it could actually get implemented. Kinda like
the fame fix (unique) that actually happened.

Why race? It is a makes RtI a good card to put into a deck that has high
level vampires, but why discard to reach it? You would only indulge in
such behaviour in a two player game. The ousting of your prey in a
multiplayer game can occur only once as a result of this card if this
fix is on, and its at the cost of one high level vampire, with at least
4 blood on them. Thats a useful weapon to blow.. only really useful as a
last ditch offensive for a VP. You actually have to think before using
it. If you equip with a soul gem in hopes of drawing the card, there is
the possibility that someone else will play the card, and you waste your
time and action. Also, the race theory is not favoured as not everyone
will put one of these cards in their deck. It will now only be a nice
accompaniment to a high level deck.

> I'm not entirely a fan of Only Usable Once Per Game cards. At least
> Ancient Influence works for everyone and Giant's Blood isn't that bad
> really.
>

I think it is a logical step from unique cards to have transient cards
played only once. Makes you think about deck design. Try to build a
degenerate deck around RtI with this fix. Errr... you can actually, but
the degeneracy will not come from RtI 8^)

> I mean a card that said
>
> "Oust a Methuselah of your choice. Only usable once per game by any
> Methuselah."
>
> would still be broken. And that wording isn't that from Return to
> Innocence really.

Yeah but at the cost of one of your vampires. Try rewording the card
Oust a methuselah of your choice, if that methuselah doesn't choose to
bounce the bleed, and if you have a day operation, and, by the way burn
the vampire that plays the card, and they have to be of very high level.
Only usable once per game by any methuselah.

It was a good idea, James.

David Naseby

Its not a random ousting. You really have to consider whether your big
vampire is better used to kill more methuselahs later or whether you can
go for the one big shot and hope you can bring another out in time to
win the game for you. You lose your big vampire, on the remote chance
that your prey cannot block or bounce the bleed. The big vampire is
still iseful, as it has at least 4 blood on it when it takes the action.
It doesn't make the card useless, but it stops RtI being a game breaker.
It evens out the cost and benefits of the card rather neatly, I think.

David Naseby

/* Note: posting from my civilian account - take
* whatever I say as if I'm just some random
* lurker - these are just my ramblings
*/

Someone (James Coupe?) pointed out that RTI is a lot like Golconda's
older brother. That got me thinking (thanks for nothing, James :-).

The effects are similar (assuming you use Golconda on your own vampire):
You lose a vampire and the pool difference between you and your prey
increases by the capacity of that vampire.

The differences:

Golconda is a Master card RTI is an action
with no cost that costs 4 blood*
with no counter except SR and can be blocked/redirected/AI'ed
that only targets 8+ cap and requires a 4+ cap

* The blood cost only serves to restrict the capacity and current
strength of the acting vampire - all blood is burned on successful
RTI / Golconda anyway.

The main effects: Prey(or redirect) loses X / you gain X - while bearing
an obvious symmetry, are not the same. Losing large amounts of pool
unexpectedly is far worse than gaining large amounts of pool when you
plan to.

Compare to Golconda used as a threat (against you Prey, e.g.):
Now, used a surprise, you prey loses a vampire and gains X ...
or pays two pool to cancel the effect entirely. (You still have
played a Master Card, of course).

Why is that last part in there? Because such a boon (X pool) with
a unplanned cost (X-cap vampire) can be detrimental enough to
unbalance the game.

How much more unbalancing is the unexpected loss of X pool (even
when your Predator loses - a planned loss - a vampire)?

The planned vs. unplanned loss of a vampire is important, of course,
for things like Soul Gem.

Other "balances" are not satisfactory:
"Block" - RTI is not a game breaker except for all the ways to
make actions unblockable running around.
"Redirect" - turns the game into roulette.
"AI" - corner case.

So anyway - am I going to get to a point any time soon?
Sure:

How about adding a sentence to RTI (borrowing from Golconda): "The
target of the bleed can pay two pool to caue the action to fail."
(the action fails - no cost is paid and the acting vampire is not
burned.)
--

had fun was in a second round, playing with a bunch of people who either a)
didn't have the money for the big cards or b) wouldn't stoop below their
principles even to win a tournament. To most people, it is obvious that RtI
and the Tomb make the game less interesting.

And to answer another criticism while I'm at it... Consider the contestation
of the Tomb. One player plays a Tomb and uses his 4 transfers. He's now
gained 1 pool and 4 transfers due to a master card with no requirements
whatsoever. This is a far better turn-around than any other card in the game.
Govern the Unaligned can give you 3 pool and 3 transfers for an action,
requiring a vampire with superior dominate, an older vampire, and an action
which can be blocked. That's the closest thing, and it has *no*
potential for further gain, whereas the Tomb could potentially give you
pool for the rest of the game. So... suppose that another player contests the
Tomb. IMO, this is a fairly stupid thing to do, as this person has spent 3
pool for a card that is useless at the moment. If player 1 wants to punish
them, it's relatively cheap to do so, or player 1 can yield the Tomb, since
he's already gotten his advantage out of it. So, in any case, player 1 wins.
Any player who is first to get out the Tomb gets an amazing advantage, and if
they yield it or let the vamp with it come into play, the next person to play
it gets a huge advantage. If you don't have a Tomb, you lose out big time.

Not only this, but this uniqueness applies to other cards as well. Hell, Art
Museum is unique. But, you say, "since Art Museum requires a clan, it's
harder to be contested." That's not a valid criticism either. Would making
Art Museum clanless make it a worse card? Of course not. If all Hunting
Grounds were clanless would they be useless? No, they'd be much easier to
use, and so Tomb is easier to use because it's clanless. Any argument so far
made in favour of the Tomb applies at least as strongly to weaker cards.
Nearly the same is true for RtI. Any bleed can be deflected or blocked. That
doesn't justify a clanless, disciplineless, +10 bleed card.

And I *do* feel violated when Arika (with her Soul Gem) bleeds me for 18 with
Day Op. Who'd like to join me in burning all Tombs and RtIs, and who has the
gasoline?

-Chris

Messages.Author: Mike Bohlmann
Messages.Body:
Personally, I think that adding fixes will only make the game
more complex and difficult to teach newbies. It doesn't make
the game very easy to learn (and will probably alienate new
players), when they play a card and are then told that that's not
how it works. I've run into that when a newbie who was obviously
self-taught tried to play a Jyhad version of Blood Fury (or Rage...
can't remember which it is) that was misprinted as a Fortitude card
instead of a Thamauturgy card. They were quite upset because they
had built their entire Gangrel deck around this misprinted card.

Now just imagine when you tell some newbie that the card text
isn't wrong, it was just changed. What would be better is to
either leave the card as is or to ban it. Explaining a banned
card is much easier than explaining why it was changed. Plus,
the banned concept is easy to grasp.

I'm not saying that RtI, TB, etc., should be banned. I'm just
saying that I don't think we should change any card's text unless
it is an errata or clarification. Personally, I think the game
would be better off without a card like RtI because when successful,
it is nearly impossible to recover from. TB and ToRIII give
advantages, but not the kind that ordinarily cause one person's
game to suddenly be over if they can't do anything about it.

Mike
